title: Layer-wise Geometric Approximation Rates for Deep Networks
abstract: arXiv:2604.20219v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Depth is widely viewed as a central contributor to the success of deep neural networks, yet standard approximation results typically give error bounds only for the final output of a network. Inspired by classical multiscale expansions and multigrade deep learning, we give depth a scale-dependent interpretation by constructing a single network whose intermediate readouts approximate the target at successively finer scales. For any $f\in L^p([0,1]^d)$ with $1\le p <\infty$ and any integer $N\ge2$, we construct a single network of width $3dN+2d+4$ with the same activation pattern in every hidden layer, using sine in the first two neurons and $\mathtt{ReLU}$ in the rest. For every $\ell\ge0$, the $L^p$ approximation error of the readout $\Phi_\ell$ at layer $\ell+4$ is bounded by $(2d+1)\omega_{f,p}(N^{-\ell})$, where $\omega_{f,p}$ denotes the $L^p$ translation modulus of $f$. Under the H\"older condition $\omega_{f,p}(t)\le Ct^\alpha$

translated_title: 深度网络的逐层几何逼近速率
translated_abstract: arXiv:2604.20219v3 公告类型：替换 摘要：深度被广泛认为是深度神经网络取得成功的核心因素，然而标准的逼近结果通常只给出网络最终输出的误差界。受经典多尺度展开与多级深度学习的启发，我们通过构造一个单一网络——其各层中间读出在逐级精细的尺度上逼近目标函数——赋予深度一个依赖于尺度的解释。对于任意 $f\in L^p([0,1]^d)$（$1\le p<\infty$）和任意整数 $N\ge2$，我们构造了一个宽度为 $3dN+2d+4$ 的单一网络，其每个隐藏层具有相同的激活模式，即前两个神经元使用正弦激活、其余使用 $\mathtt{ReLU}$ 激活。对每个 $\ell\ge0$，第 $\ell+4$ 层读出 $\Phi_\ell$ 的 $L^p$ 逼近误差被 $(2d+1)\omega_{f,p}(N^{-\ell})$ 所界定，其中 $\omega_{f,p}$ 表示 $f$ 的 $L^p$ 平移模。在 Hölder 条件 $\omega_{f,p}(t)\le Ct^\alpha$ 下……
tldr: 本文构造了一个宽度为 $3dN+2d+4$、各隐藏层激活模式完全相同的单一深度网络，其逐层中间读出以由目标函数 $L^p$ 平移模（Hölder 条件下为 $O(N^{-\alpha\ell})$）控制的速率在逐级精细的尺度上逼近目标，从而为网络深度赋予了尺度依赖的全新解释。
en_tdlr: This paper constructs a single deep network of width 3dN+2d+4 with identical activation patterns across all hidden layers, whose intermediate readouts approximate the target at successively finer scales with layer-wise errors bounded by the L^p translation modulus (O(N^{-αℓ}) under Hölder smoothness), thereby giving network depth a scale-dependent interpretation.
